newsitem.title: MALAYSIA: Jardine Fleming says planning first Malaysian fund.
newsitem.headline: Jardine Fleming says planning first Malaysian fund.

text.p: Fund manager Jardine Fleming said on Thursday it will soon launch its first unit trust fund in Malaysia through its local joint venture.
The open-ended fund could be launched as soon as next month if approvals from the Securities Commission came through, said Simon Crinage, chief executive of Jardine Fleming Apex Unit Trusts Bhd.
"We want this to be our flagship product. It will be a Malaysian equity (fund)," he told reporters.
He said more funds would be launched later.
"We have a structured plan for a series of products," Crinage said.
He declined to give further details of the issue.
"I would be delighted if we get off to a start with anything above 50 million ringgit," he said in reply to a question.
He said the first unit trust fund will be a mix, targetted at both individuals and corporate bodies.
He said the Jardine Fleming Malaysia Trust fund, a Hong Kong-based product, had averaged a growth of 25 percent a year over the last five years.
Another fund, the Jardine Fleming Eastern Trust fund, grew at an average 27 percent a year over the same period.

He said there were some redemptions from the Hong Kong-based Malaysian fund in the last two months due to a currency crisis that has pulled down the ringgit, but that there was no withdrawal by Jardine from the country.
"We have seen redemptions from the Jardine Fleming Malaysia Trust," he said. "Fundamentally Malaysia is very attractive."
He said a strong earnings growth projected for local companies was expected to keep the Kuala Lumpur stock market buoyant in the long-term.
"We are looking at possible 14 percent growth a year for the next five years," he said.
